name: Green Lantern Power Ring
summary: A ring forged by the Guardians of the Universe that turns its wearer's willpower into solid green light. Test pilot Hal Jordan got his from a dying alien and joined an interstellar police force.

parts.label: Band
parts.fact: In Showcase #22 (1959) the alien Lantern Abin Sur crash-lands on Earth, and his ring seeks out a fearless successor nearby: test pilot Hal Jordan.

parts.label: Green lens
parts.fact: The ring shapes green energy into constructs of any form the wearer can imagine, plus force fields that let a Lantern fly and survive in open space.

parts.label: Power battery
parts.fact: In the Silver Age the ring ran dry after 24 hours and was topped up at a lantern-shaped battery, itself tied to the giant Central Power Battery on the planet Oa.

parts.label: Charge & oath
parts.fact: Lanterns often recite an oath while recharging, though it is optional. The famous verse is usually credited to SF author Alfred Bester in the 1940s, a claim he later disputed.

trivia: The first Green Lantern, Alan Scott, debuted in All-American Comics #16 (1940) with a magic ring; Hal's 1959 version swapped magic for alien science.
Early rings could not affect anything yellow. The 2005 Rebirth story explained it as the fear monster Parallax trapped inside the Central Battery.
For years the rings were also coded so the wearer could not kill; the Guardians lifted that rule during the Sinestro Corps war of 2007.
The Corps splits the universe into 3,600 sectors, with Earth's sector numbered 2814.
